If your brief is “surreal/editorial, but commercially clear,” I’d look at Toronto studios that combine art direction with positioning and messaging—not just visual design.

Jacknife — A strong fit if you want concept-driven brand work that still has a strategic backbone. Their work spans brand strategy, identity, packaging, campaigns, digital and environmental design.

Concrete Design Communications — Particularly interesting if you want sophisticated visual language plus campaign, photography and art direction. Their process can run from positioning/voice through execution.

Blok Design — Worth considering for a more design-led, editorial sensibility. They combine positioning and naming with identity, packaging, books/editorial, digital and spatial work.

WHITMAN EMORSON — Especially relevant if editorial is central to the aesthetic. They have capabilities in custom publishing and branded content alongside broader brand systems.

Chargefield — An interesting option if the surreal side of your brief leans toward cinematic, art-directed campaign imagery. They're particularly focused on key art and entertainment-style campaign creative.

Made by Emblem — Their Toronto studio focuses on hospitality and arts/culture, with concept-driven identities, campaigns, editorial design, illustration and experiential work. 
Made by Emblem

Gooseberry Studios — More photography/brand-world oriented: they explicitly combine brand strategy with art-directed commercial and editorial photography. 
Gooseberry Studios

For the “make it beautiful without making the offer mysterious” part, I'd specifically ask prospective marketers to show you a case where they translated a distinctive visual concept into a clear positioning statement, offer architecture, landing page and campaign CTA. That will tell you more than a surreal portfolio alone.

If you tell me what your Toronto business sells + approximate marketing budget, I can narrow this to 3–5 firms that match the actual offer and scale.
